items.title: How to get Tifa and Barret's outfits in FFXIV
items.content:
By Paulo Kawanishi Published Oct 28, 2026, 1:50 PM EDT Guides How fast can you type "Nibelheim"?

Image: Square Enix via Polygon Add Polygon.com on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover Summary Generate a summary of this story Jump links Jump Links How to get Tifa and Barret's outfits in FFXIV How to start the Keybound Brawler event in FFXIV All FFXIV Keybound Brawler rewards Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Tifa and Barret's outfits are the real stars in Final Fantasy 14 ' s event in the Keybound Brawlers , a new collaboration with Final Fantasy 7 . Unlike Cloud's outfit, which is based on the Final Fantasy 7: Advent Children design and has been in the game for ages, these two are based on the FF7 remake project. To get them and many other FF7 -themed cosmetics and items, you must survive the typing brawls and earn a special currency.

Below, you can find all the information you need to learn how to get Tifa and Barret's outfits in FFXIV .

You can only obtain Tifa and Barret's outfit by participating in the Keybound Brawler event , which runs from Oct. 28, until the release of Final Fantasy 14 's patch 8.0 with the Evercold expansion (which should be in January).

The only prerequisites for participating in the event are reaching level 15 , completing one of the following main scenario quests: "The Gridanian Envoy," "The Ul'dahn Envoy," or "The Lominsan Envoy", and unlocking the Gold Saucer . As one might expect given the name, you also need a keyboard to play this game.

Image: Square Enix via Polygon By winning matches during the event, you earn the Manderville Gold Saucer Credits (MGC), which you can exchange for the outfits at the MGC Trader in the Keybound Square. This currency is different from the Manderville Gold Saucer Points (MGP), which you obtain by participating in the regular Gold Saucer's activities.

To purchase all four pieces of Tifa's outfit , you will need 1,380 MGC , and for Barret's five pieces , you'll need 1,570 MGC (I'm not considering both the Avalanche Brawler's Earring and the Avalanche Leader's Earring in these sums). If you complete all three waves of a brawl, you can earn from 200-340 MGC depending on your final score . This means that you will need six to 12 matches to earn enough credits to purchase all the pieces of both outfits.

Keep in mind that the outfits are gender locked when deciding which ones to prioritize.

Graphic: Paulo Kawanishi/Polygon | Source images: Square Enix via Polygon While the Keybound Brawler event is taking place, you can start it by traveling to the Gold Saucer in Thanalan and talking to the Catlike Mammet (5.4, 7.0) to accept the "Keyward Bound" side quest .

Next, you will need to talk to W'zazanh at the Wonder Square (6.1, 7.3) to enter the Keybound Square. Once inside, interact with the Magitype Master behind the counter to complete the quest. Since there are no crystals to teleport to the area, you will always need to talk to W'zazanh to return the Keybound Square in the future.

Graphic: Paulo Kawanishi/Polygon | Source images: Square Enix via Polygon To play Keybound Brawler matches, you need to talk to the Keybound Registrar NPC (5.8, 6.0) . While it's possible to queue as a group, you can also go solo and wait for the game to find party members for you.

Each match is divided into three waves, during which enemies will try to approach the barrier in front of your party. If they reach it, enemies will attack the barrier, lowering your party's HP bar. To attack them, you must correctly type the words that appear above them. Pay attention because, although you don't need to distinguish between uppercase and lowercase, both punctuation and accents count . If enemies deplete your party's HP bar, you will fail the brawl.

Image: Square Enix via Polygon By simply participating in a match, you will earn some MGC, but your score and the number of waves you survive affect the final amount. If you complete the last wave, in addition to MGC and MGP, you also earn a keybound coffer . These can contain various rewards, from food to weapons like the Adamant Rod.

The Keybound Brawler event offers all kinds of rewards, ranging from the two Tifa and Barret's outfits to the unique mount Magitek Scorpion. You can only obtain these rewards by exchanging MGC except for the aforementioned coffers, which you also earn whenever you defeat the third wave's boss.

items.title: Final Fantasy XIV Beastmasters Can Compete For Rewards & Glory, Type for FFVII Goodies, and Are We Closer to Butt Sliders?
Final Fantasy 14 devs say Evercold's new Evolved mode isn't massive power creep: "If you don't want to change, you don't have to"
items.content:

(Image credit: Square Enix) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter It's no secret that Final Fantasy 14 is scrapping its infamous two-minute meta and adopting an entirely new job system, Evolved, come Evercold this winter – but just how different will that system play, and how much more damage will it allow for?

As a hardcore raider myself, one thing about Evercold has been heavy on my mind since the expansion's reveal at Fan Fest this summer: the introduction of the Reborn and Evolved job systems, with the latter being entirely new to the MMO. The reason it's been heavy on my mind is simple – Square Enix implied that the Evolved system, which rearranges our class skills into a simpler, neater format, hotbar-wise, will let us deal more damage.

Michael-Christopher Koji Fox, localization lead, lays out the differences between the Reborn system – which is essentially what we're playing with now – and Evolved in a new interview with content creators Sarah Jane, Kwisty, and Pezz on YouTube , though, and I'm slightly less concerned now... I think. He describes a bit of what we already know (e.g. the fact that Evercold's debut jobs, the Bastion and mystery DPS, won't have a Reborn mode) first, assuring fans, "If you don't want to change, you don't have to."

Watch On The thing is, though, those of us who engage in Ultimates and other "hard" content might feel the need to if the Reborn mode – the original system – is capable of less damage… right? Well, according to Fox, not exactly: "I don't think it's like, 'Okay, this Evolved mode is going to do 50% more damage.' I think it's going to be very negligible." That's a relief – right? And, it all boils down to how different the Reborn and Evolved systems are.

"I think it's just because the modes are so different and some of the skill rotations are going to be so different that damage will be dealt in different ways," as Fox states. "That might end up affecting" damage throughout a fight, but it shouldn't matter in terms of ability to clear and all that. "It's not going to be something that's going to be a deal breaker," as Square Enix wants "to keep it as small as possible." But it was "unavoidable" altogether, as the modes can't play the same way – unavoidable, but again, negligible. I doubt that Fox's words are enough to satisfy most raiders, however, sadly, knowing how highly regarded parses are (and likely always will be). Should the Evolved version of one's abilities allow for even the slightest, ittiest-bittiest boost in damage, they'll probably opt to abandon the trusty ol' Reborn mode – ask me how I know.

Final Fantasy 14 devs beg players to "take time to read" the MMO's options before Evercold is out Final Fantasy 14 lead Yoshi-P would "tackle completely new game designs" if he made another MMO Final Fantasy 14 fans spot Evercold character in Patch 7.56 screenshots, theorize new DPS class I'm not sure what I'll choose myself just yet, as an Astrologian. I'll have to wait and see what the promised healer changes will look like before I do – keeping tanks alive, damage dealers buffed, and DOTs up is tricky enough as it is.

Final Fantasy Resonance Sets New Steam Record for Single-Player Final Fantasy Games
items.summary: Final Fantasy Resonance has surpassed 42,000 concurrent players on Steam, setting a new peak for a single-player Final Fantasy game.
items.content:
Final Fantasy Resonance has surpassed 42,000 concurrent players on Steam, setting a new peak for a single-player entry in Square Enix’s long-running RPG franchise. The game launched globally on October 22, 2026, and has already drawn a substantial audience on PC.

The new milestone puts Final Fantasy Resonance ahead of Final Fantasy VII Rebirth, which previously held the record for the highest peak concurrent player count among the franchise’s single-player games on Steam, with more than 40,000 players. Other recent entries, including Final Fantasy XV and Final Fantasy XVI, recorded lower peaks of approximately 29,500 and 27,500 players, respectively.

items.title: Final Fantasy 14 Players Deliver Perfect Response to 2026’s PHP Vulnerability
items.summary: Warriors of Light across the world proved, once again, why the MMO's community is special
items.content:
By Willa Rowe Published Oct 24, 2026, 5:05 AM EDT Willa Rowe is a contributing writer at Polygon, covering games and entertainment. She is a New York-based journalist and critic whose work has been featured in Kotaku, Digital Trends, the A.V. Club, GamesRadar+, and more. She also co-hosts the Girl Mode podcast. News Warriors of Light across the world proved, once again, why the MMO's community is special

Add Polygon.com on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover Sign in to your Polygon.com account Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread 2 Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap A number of major websites and services went offline earlier this week thanks to a massive PHP security vulnerability . One such service was Final Fantasy 14 . That posed a major problem for plants. You see, Square Enix's MMO has a number of systems on real-world timers that continue regardless of whether a player is logged in. Those unlucky enough to be locked out of the game during the PHP issue were left fearing that their gardens would wither and die. Thankfully, the community stepped in.

Final Fantasy 14 did not shut down completely across the globe, meaning some players were still able to wander Eorzea. These players took it upon themselves to lend a helping hand. One such player made a post on Reddit (spotted by PC Gamer ) that simply offered " PHP Watering Service ." It was exactly what it sounded like. The player invited others to reply or DM with the location of their in-game home so they could, at no cost, water plants for those in need.

Image: Square Enix via Polygon Other players had similar ideas, with more watering service posts popping up on X . Mechanically, this is all possible because of a neat feature of the MMO. There is no special requirement for watering plants, and players can water any plant in the game, even those in other players' homes. This created a communal aid network across the internet that allowed everyone's plants to stay hydrated and healthy. It's just one example of how Warriors of Light are willing to help each other out in the most unexpected ways. There is a reason why Final Fantasy 14 's community has such a good reputation.

After roughly 24 hours of frantic work on the PHP issue, Square Enix has started allowing new logins . That means players should be able to get back to Eorzea and begin taking care of their plants themselves. As the PHP security vulnerability only lasted about one day, nobody's plants should have died.

While the game being back online is a good thing, it does come with one caveat. Square Enix briefly paused housing auto-demolition, which reclaims inactive housing plots if the owner fails to access the building within a certain time limit. That system exists because Final Fantasy 14 's housing is not instanced, meaning there is only a finite number of plots per server. Now that the PHP issues are solved, auto-demolition will resume on Oct. 26.

Websites and services ranging from 4Chan to Spotify are all at risk

items.title: How a data centre united Australia's gaming community
items.source: ABC News & Headlines – Australian Broadcasting Corporation
items.summary: After years of playing on distant worlds, Australian gamers of the popular Japanese role-playing game Final Fantasy XIV discovered a new home. Now that community has welcomed the game developers Down Under.
items.content:
Michael-Christopher Koji Fox (left) and Toshio Murouchi (right) were the main attractions for players at PAX Australia. ( Supplied: Square Enix )

Link copied Share Share article Before the Oceania data centre arrived, Australians sometimes found the online role-playing game Final Fantasy XIV a surprisingly lonely multiplayer experience.

On the Asia server, they'd struggle to find enough fellow English speakers to tackle the game's notorious super-bosses. Those visiting American servers would find the in-game Golden Saucer amusement park sparsely populated during another time zone's twilight hours.

And the few who chose the most distant Europe server struggled with "input lag" that perilously delayed gameplay actions, with the risk of failed quests and let-down teammates.

That changed in January 2022, 12 years after the game was released, when, encouraged by a pandemic boom in player numbers, developer Square Enix finally launched Oceania servers. It was a decision that united players in the region.

Lin, a Final Fantasy XIV community organiser from Melbourne, was shocked at the scale of the local player base.

"When they finally released a server where our ping [internet connection latency speed] was manageable, we were like, 'whoa, there's thousands of people here'," they tell ABC Arts.

"It took 30 minutes just to get into the queue. You no longer had to guess if we could speak the same language or understand the same lingo."

Final Fantasy's near-40-year legacy lured Pat, another community organiser from Melbourne, into online role-playing games.

"I love the Final Fantasy series. That's the one I grew up with," they say.

The Final Fantasy series has nabbed more than 212 million sales. ( Supplied: Square Enix )

By nature, Final Fantasy XIV's community primarily exists online. A community organisation called Jjammin' runs in-game award shows, theatre shows and musical productions throughout the year.

For many in the region's broader Final Fantasy XIV community, the annual Limsa Extreme meet-up at PAX Australia, one of the country's biggest exhibitions of games and gaming culture, is the highlight on the calendar.

Limsa Extreme was created in 2022 by head organiser Kiya, who was determined to make up for the absence of official events and meetups in Australia. Since then, the event has drawn players from across ANZ, Malaysia and Indonesia, and now even the Japan-based developers.

items.title: Final Fantasy XIV Diesel Apparel and Merchandise Revealed
items.summary: Italian brand Diesel has released a new Final Fantasy XIV-themed collection of apparel and merchandise in Japan.
items.content:
A new merchandise lineup based on Square Enix’s Final Fantasy XIV has appeared courtesy of the Italian brand Diesel. The latter revealed it via its Japanese official website and social media account .

The premium brand sells a variety of items ranging from apparel to necklaces and phone cases. However, all of them cost more than ¥10,000. The most affordable ones are moulded cases for the regular and Pro versions of iPhone 17, both of which have the same price tag of ¥11,000 (~$69.80). Meanwhile, the most expensive item in this lineup is the FF-D-Barus Jacket , which costs a whopping ¥132,000 (~$837.85).

The median price of this collection is ¥23,100 (~$146.50), which falls on the T-Norm shirts with ten different back designs available. These designs are also available to view right below:

This collaboration adds yet another entry to the list of merchandise collections based on Final Fantasy XIV . In August 2026, Square Enix released the Emet Selch Earring and perfumes inspired by 21 in-game jobs. It also worked with its subsidiary Taito to bring back the Mini Lamp Quest icon magnets as arcade prizes, as well as Suntory to sell cans with sticker labels featuring the MMORPG’s characters via vending machines.

The Diesel x Final Fantasy XIV Capsule Collection merchandise is now available in Japan. The items are based on the MMORPG readily accessible worldwide on PC, PlayStation 5, PlayStation 4, Xbox Series X, and Switch 2 .

items.title: 24-Year-Old Final Fantasy MMORPG Finally Gets A Generous Free Trial
items.summary: Those looking to jump into Final Fantasy XI can now access the entire base game without time restrictions
items.content:
Final Fantasy XI Final Fantasy XIV Square Enix

Final Fantasy XI rarely gets any updates these days, but fans still have a ton of love for Square Enix’s first attempt at turning its hit RPG franchise into an online behemoth. Now the game that began life on the PlayStation 2 is getting a more generous free trial nearly a quarter century later.

The 2002 release of Final Fantasy XI aimed to exploit the then-booming MMO craze alongside hits like World of Warcraft . Final Fantasy XIV , while not quite as popular today as it was at its peak, has enjoyed ongoing success which has helped revitalize interest in Square Enix’s first MMORPG. The 2002 game is certainly dated by modern standards, but newcomers now have a fresh reason to experience its old-fashioned gameplay sensibilities thanks to a revamped free trial that ditches time limits and raises the level cap to 75.

The game was first released as an online-only PS2 MMORPG before being ported to PC months later, with an Xbox 360 version eventually being released in 2006. Services for both console versions endured until 2016. Since the game’s initial release, there have been no fewer than five expansion packs and eight additional scenarios, with the latest released just a few years ago. The game even saw a boost in players in 2025 thanks to new quests in Final Fantasy XIV that tied back into the narrative of the original game.

But though long-time fans continued to trudge along with the game, the free trial was so stingy compared to the one offered by FFXIV that players would often meme about the discrepancy. Unlike the high level cap with no time restrictions and free access to story content across multiple expansions offered for XIV , the free trial for XI previously only allowed players to level a single character to 50, with a time limit of just 14 days before a paid subscription was needed. Both requirements have now been relaxed .

Not everything is open to free players. The free trial still limits you to the base game content only, and your account can’t hold more than 100,000 gil (in-game currency) at any one time. You’re also not allowed to trade or use the in-game auction house to acquire equipment and items. While you can join a party of other players, you can’t create one.

Personally, I just find it impressive that a PS2-era MMO like Final Fantasy XI is still able to find an audience. Changes like these can only help the game to continue finding success, perhaps for another 20 or more years. Maybe.
